messages.subject: random questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I have some random questions about using Rqtl that I thought I'd throw
out.
If anyone can help out please drop me a note.

Does anyone know how to tell what version of RQTL you are working with?
 I'd like to make sure that my updating in "R" has worked.

Does a "scantwo" analysis only work under a "normal" distribution
model?  If not, are there plans to extend the scantwo analysis to
include other distributions?

Is there a simply way to make a scatterplot of pairs of phenotypes in
"R" using an Rqtl data file?

Is there a simply way to make transformations of phenotypes?

Thanks for the help
Tom

messages.subject: Re: random questions
messages.body_plain:
> Does anyone know how to tell what version of RQTL you are working with?
>  I'd like to make sure that my updating in "R" has worked.

In the latest versions, you can type qtlversion().
Alternatively, if you type help(library=qtl) the first bit tells the
version installed.

> Does a "scantwo" analysis only work under a "normal" distribution
> model?  If not, are there plans to extend the scantwo analysis to
> include other distributions?

Yes, and eventually.  It does also work for binary traits
(model="binary").

> Is there a simply way to make a scatterplot of pairs of phenotypes in
> "R" using an Rqtl data file?

pairs(mycross$pheno)

> Is there a simply way to make transformations of phenotypes?

If you want to use the log (base 2) of phenotype 1, type

   mycross$pheno[,1] <- log2(mycross$pheno[,1])

cheers,
karl

messages.subject: plotting scanone
messages.body_plain:

the plot(lod1trait) statement.

Tom
messages.body_snippet:
Does anyone know how to add a label at the x-axis of a LOD plot using
the plot(lod1trait) statement.

Tom

messages.subject: Re: plotting scanone
messages.body_plain:
At this point, we don't have an easy way to modify the x- and y-axis
labels.

The y-axis label comes from the name of the third column in your
"lod1trait"
output.  You could change it to "LOD score" by typing:

   colnames(lod1trait)[3] <- "LOD score"

The x-axis label is pre-coded to be blank if multiple chromosomes are
plotted
(and in which case, there are chromosome labels) and is "Map position
(cM)"
if a single chromosome is plotted.

The only way to change those x-axis label choices is to modify the
plot.scanone
function itself.  You can save the function to a file:

   dput(plot.scanone, file="myplotscanone.R")

and then modify that code.  If you type "plot.scanone <-" at the very
top
of that file, and then load it into R using source("myplotscanone.R")
your new version will override the previous version.

When I'm making publication-quality plots, I usually modify the R/qtl
plot
functions in that sort of way.

karl

messages.subject_clean: using sim.geno with the binary model
messages.body_plain:
We've not yet implemented the fit of models with binary
phenotypes by imputation, and it's not high on my priority
list.

Could you give further details about why you "could
not produce the right graph"?

For scanone with the binary model, you need to first run
calc.genoprob() to calculate genotype probabilities.  Had
you done that?

Kind regards,
karl

messages.subject: Re: Calculation of variance explained by a QTL
messages.subject_clean: Calculation of variance explained by a QTL
messages.body_plain:
We don't have a function to do this.  But the percent variance explained
by a QTL, in the context of a single-QTL model, can be calculated from
the
LOD score by the following formula:

   Percent variance explained = 100 ( 1 - 10^(-2 LOD / n) )

where n is the sample size.

karl
